title: Therapy Expectation Optimisation (TEO) - A Randomised Controlled Trial on the Impact of Expectations in Psychotherapy
summary:
The TEO-Study aims to examine the efficacy of an individualised, expectation-focused, single-session psychological intervention including two telephone booster consultations (optimized psychotherapy information (OPTI) consultation), which aims to positively impact treatment expectations regarding outpatient psychotherapy, thereby enhancing its' efficacy. To this end, treatment expectations and psychopathological distress will be assessed before and during outpatient psychotherapy.
We hypothesize that participants in the intervention group will demonstrate a greater reduction in psychopathological distress and depressive symptoms, as well as a greater increase in mental well-being. Additionally, we assume that more positive and less negative treatment expectations are associated with less psychopathological distress and depressive symptoms, as well as greater mental well-being. Furthermore, we hypothesize that participation in the OPTI consultation will lead to an increase in positive and a decrease in negative expectations. Finally, we assume that individual differences in treatment expectations before starting psychotherapy are accounted for by previous treatment experiences and the presence of trauma.
Adults (minimum aged 18) who are starting outpatient psychotherapy following an initial psychotherapeutic consultation are eligible to participate. Half of the participants will receive the OPTI consultation. The study will take place over a period of 9–12 months before the start and over the course of outpatient psychotherapy. During this period, participants will be asked to complete five online questionnaires.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use
Behavioural syndromes associated with physiological disturbances and physical factors
Disorders of adult personality and behaviour

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimum age of 18 years,
Email account and internet-enabled device,
Scheduled on a waiting list or just begun outpatient psychotherapy following a psychotherapeutic consultation (indication for psychotherapy due to the presence of at least one mental disorder in an outpatient setting),
Informed consent to participate in the study and consent to data processing.
Exclusion criteria:
Currently ongoing outpatient psychotherapy with 3 or more sessions already completed,
insufficient German language skills for the planned standardised assessments,
insufficient cognitive abilities for the assessments (e.g. due to severe IQ impairment, neurological disease or intoxication, to be assessed in the screening interview), current suicidality (i.e. suicidal thoughts within the last week).
